parts.text: During her science class study, Brady discovered that each whale in the sea has 40 gallons of blood.
She also found out that a shark has three times as much blood as a whale.
In the same class, she learned that a dolphin has half the blood volume of a whale, but this information is not relevant to her current calculations.
Brady is now curious to find out the total number of gallons of blood that ten sharks swimming in the sea would have.
Can you help her with this calculation?

parts.text: Every day, a bakery makes 60 bread loaves.
In the morning, they manage to sell two-thirds of these loaves.
The remaining loaves are then divided equally and sold in the afternoon and evening.
Can you determine how many loaves of bread are sold in the afternoon?

parts.text: Julie operates the cash register exactly twice as fast as her less-experienced colleague Jewel.
Daily, Jewel processes 50 customers.
However, on Wednesdays, Jewel processes 10% fewer customers due to a shorter work shift.
What is the total weekly production for the two if they work all days of the week?

parts.text: Stephen borrowed $300 from his sister and promised to return it with an additional 2% of the money he owed.
To make things more interesting, he decided to pay her back in a unique way.
For 11 months, Stephen will give his sister $25 per month, even though he also spends $50 on his hobby of collecting rare coins each month.
On the twelfth month, he will pay the remaining amount, including the interest, and also plans to buy a coin worth $100.
How much will Stephen pay his sister in the twelfth month, excluding his coin purchases?
